dedupe_keys.name: risk evaluation of autonomous vehicle integration in traffic environments

description: The author-institution and DOI-bound publication abstracts establish an analytic-hierarchy model evaluating hazard, vulnerability and exposure for autonomous-vehicle integration. The IN2CCAM case covers urban and extra-urban traffic and defines indicator weights; accident probability has the greatest weight in the reported assessment. Social acceptance, production cost and charging constraints also enter the model. It is an applied risk model, with specific locations, input weights and executable access unknown. The source authors provide the native description and file descriptors through Zenodo. Only metadata was inspected; no measurements, archives, source code or document bodies were retrieved. Public access and the deposit document licence do not establish executable access, software reuse rights or operating costs. Coverage remains bounded to the named experiments, with other geographic and temporal fields unknown. Related project resources may overlap; common project membership does not establish identical simulation inputs or results.
name: Risk Evaluation of Autonomous Vehicle Integration in Traffic Environments
